core_conclusions: Arbitrary group-action orbit intersection is equivalent to intersection of the first-coordinate fibers under the stated base intersection hypothesis.
The one-sided normalizer condition identifies those fibers with actual variance subgroups; it does not supply transitivity of their mix.
C\W/V gives a sufficient list of flag tests. One flag suffices when W=CV, or when the mix itself is medial-section-transitive.
The six-coordinate construction gives six polytopal covers with 360 flags each; two compatible rootings mix to a 1080-flag nonpolytope despite passing the proposed base test.
The eleven-cell and four-simplex are actual regular inputs, with coprime middle labels and orientable second input, whose mix has an end intersection of order60 rather than30.
The stated parity, facet-cover, common-quotient and regular-core consequences follow with their actual rooted embeddings.
The explicit affine example is a genuine two-orbit four-polytope of class 2_{1,2}, with144flags, uniform facets and vertex figures, and medial digons and triangles.

Its2592-flag mix with the other rooted copy is regular, polytopal and the smallest regular cover. The six variance groups are identified inside one actual automorphism group. Their two required intersections have orders3 and2, while the intersection of the two medial variance groups is trivial.
